newsitem.title: INDIA: India detains pro-democracy Bhutanese activist.
newsitem.headline: India detains pro-democracy Bhutanese activist.

text.p: India has detained a pro-democracy activist from Bhutan after Thimpu demanded his extradition from New Delhi, Indian officials said on Friday.
They told Reuters that the man, whose name was only given as "Dorji", was taken into police custody late last month after objections from Bhutan over his political activities in India.

Bhutanese King Jigme Singye Wangchuck's government has been locked in a struggle against ethnic Nepalis living in the country, accusing them of seeking to destabilise the tiny landlocked Himalayan state.
Indian officials said Bhutan was also worried over a growing demand for democracy by ethnic Bhutanese.
Bhutanese embassy officials could not be reached for comment.
Relations between India and Bhutan are governed by a treaty that gives New Delhi a major say in Thimpu's foreign affairs and security matters.
But New Delhi is also wary of repatriating "Dorji" to Bhutan, fearing repercussions from its own human rights groups, officials said.
